basis: Heterogeneous nuclear-lamina disease umbrella with prominent muscle and skeletal disorders; cardiac, metabolic and neurologic disease varies by subtype.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: cardiomyopathy and conduction disease characterize particular laminopathies, not most patients across this broad umbrella.

basis: Cerebral vasculopathy, brain injury and ocular dysgenesis define the spectrum; myopathy and renal pathology are subtype-dependent without established umbrella-wide frequency.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: myopathy is recognized, especially in particular COL4A1 phenotypes, but involvement in at least 30% across COL4A1/A2 disorders is not established.

basis: Demyelinating neuropathy with characteristic progressive deafness (3/3); lasting foot deformities 2/2 and muscle atrophy support musculoskeletal involvement. Glaucoma is separate.

decisions.ocular: none: glaucoma in 2/3 is a separately diagnosed association; intrinsic ocular damage from CMT4D is not established.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: neurogenic muscle atrophy and persistent skeletal deformities are common; pes cavus 2/2 and claw hands/hammertoes 2/3.
decisions.otologic: primary: progressive sensorineural deafness is a defining feature of this subtype, reported in 3/3 and typically developing by adulthood.

basis: Lysosomal storage disease defined by neurologic dysfunction and characteristic retinal disease with progressive visual loss; skeletal and visceral disease chiefly characterize type II.

decisions.neurologic: primary: myoclonus and progressive neurologic dysfunction in type I, and developmental impairment in type II, are central defining manifestations.
decisions.ocular: primary: characteristic macular disease and progressive visual loss are central diagnostic manifestations, rather than incidental deposits alone.

basis: Sensory-autonomic neuropathy with defining sweat-function loss; corneal scarring occurs in 15/20 (75%). Recurrent skin infections are secondary.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: hypohidrosis is a named, defining loss of cutaneous sweat function, present in 9/20; its autonomic origin does not remove the skin manifestation.

basis: Developmental impairment 6/6; atrial septal defect and persistent ptosis each 3/6 support involvement. Hypoglycemia 3/6 lacks evidence of persistent metabolic dysfunction.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: hypoglycemia occurs in 3/6, but the supplied evidence does not establish recurrent or lasting intrinsic endocrine/metabolic dysfunction.

basis: Syndromic hypothyroidism 3/3, arthritis 2/2 and recurrent aphthous ulceration 2/2 support involvement. Respiratory infections and their separate sequelae are excluded; small cohort.

decisions.pulmonary: none: bronchiectasis in 1/1 is a separately diagnosed sequel of recurrent respiratory infection, rather than established direct pulmonary autoimmunity.
decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: recurrent aphthous stomatitis in 2/2 represents intrinsic immune-mediated oral mucosal ulceration; mouth belongs to this axis.

basis: Disordered bone mineralization and remodeling define this metabolic bone disease; chronic kidney disease is its separately diagnosed underlying cause.

decisions.renal: none: kidney disease causes the osteodystrophy; osteodystrophy does not itself directly damage the kidneys.

basis: Fatal hepatic failure 3/3; renal anomalies, pulmonary lymphangiectasia and VSD 80-99%. Polydactyly 80-99% and protein-losing enteropathy 30-79% omitted at cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: ventricular septal defect occurs in 80-99%, supporting structural cardiac involvement independently of lymphatic abnormalities.
decisions.pulmonary: primary: pulmonary lymphangiectasia occurs in 80-99% and is a major organ manifestation of the defining lymphatic malformation.
decisions.renal: primary: renal anomalies are explicitly defining, with abnormal renal morphology and hydronephrosis reported in 80-99%.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none at cap: defining polydactyly occurs in 80-99%, but hepatic, renal, pulmonary and cardiac disease carry greater functional severity.

basis: Intellectual and speech developmental impairment define the disorder. Extra-neural findings reported in isolated 1/1 assessments do not establish ≥30% prevalence in the ≥6-person cohort.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: cleft palate and ankyloglossia each have only 1/1 assessed reports; common intrinsic oral disease across the larger cohort is not established.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: skeletal abnormalities each have isolated 1/1 reports; overlap and population frequency are unknown, so ≥30% involvement is unproven.
decisions.otologic: none: conductive hearing impairment is reported in 1/1 assessed patient, insufficient to establish ≥30% prevalence across the larger cohort.
